Fully automated regression analysis and log processing with a shell script

Source: vignettes/articles/phyreg_shell_project.Rmd
phyreg_shell_project.Rmd


The main goal of the InNOutBT package is to readily create input data and process output data for Meade & Pagel’s (2022) BayesTraits program.

Here in this article, we show how to use InNOutBT’s function shell.phyreg.proj for a full shell script run and log processing of multiple phylogenetic regression analyses with Meade & Pagel’s (2022) BayesTraits program. By reporting a directory path and the computer’s operating system (“unix” or “windows”), this function creates the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project with associated example scripts.

The available example of a shell script in Unix or Windows PowerShell helps to fully automate both the complete BayesTraits regression analyses and the processing of the resulting log and stones files, by automatically running the three main InNOutBT functions phyreg.inputs, phyreg.shell, and phyreg.outputs, without directly opening the R or RStudio programs.

Note that the BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project folder that comes with InNOutBT package was originally used in our recently published specific study on the ecological diversification of the Vataireoid legumes. So, you will have to edit the folder paths and analysis parameters in these example scripts according to your desired regression analyses. See the associated articles on how to set the parameters to create input files with phyreg.inputs for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to create the internal shell script with phyreg.shell for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to process the resulting output files with phyreg.outputs. You might also want to see the BayesTraits 5.0.3 Manual for further details on each of BayesTraits parameters available for phylogenetic regressions so as to better understand how to set the arguments available in the InNOutBT functions.

Setup

InNOutBT is not on CRAN yet, but you can install the latest development version from GitHub:

#install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/InNOutBT")
library(InNOutBT)


Creating a Unix shell project folder

The shell.phyreg.proj function is very simple and has only two arguments. By just setting any path on your computer and the argument syst = "unix", you can readily create the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project with associated example files (R scripts, shell script, and data folder) for running the phylogenetic regressions of the Vataireoid legumes on macOS Monterey. But then you can easily modify such available scripts for your specific analyses.

library(InNOutBT)

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = "/Users/domingoscardoso",
                  syst = "unix")

After running the shell.phyreg.proj function, it will readily create the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project, a data folder with the input data files vataireoids_1610_25May2022_BayesTraits.csv and vatcomb30_24May22_Yule.con.tree, as well as the main shell script BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh and R scripts 1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R, 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, and 3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R.



You should see the associated articles on how to set the parameters to create input files with phyreg.inputs for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to create the internal shell script with phyreg.shell for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to process the resulting output files with phyreg.outputs. In these articles, you will find how to fully edit the R scripts 1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R, 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, and 3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R according to your particular study. Otherwise, if you run the example files with the same parameter settings, you will be able to fully reproduce the analysis of our Vataireoid legume study.

The main shell script file BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh performs the full phylogenetic regression analysis and processing of results. Its first lines hold the paths to your folders, as shown in the image below, which you will set in the next section. The path in the image is an example from an earlier version of BayesTraits, so yours will be different.



Running the Unix shell script

You will work with two folders: the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project and the folder where the BayesTraits executable file is installed. You always start the analysis from the project folder. You do not need to open the BayesTraits folder, because the main shell script moves there by itself to run the analyses, and then brings the results back to the project folder.

Before the first run

1. Download and install BayesTraits in any folder. Note the path to that folder and the name of the executable file, such as BayesTraitsV5.

2. Check that the executable file starts, by running its full path in the Terminal. If it starts and keeps waiting, press Control + C to leave it.

/Users/yourname/BayesTraits/BayesTraitsV5

If macOS stops the program, for instance with the message killed or a warning that it cannot be opened, this is because macOS blocks programs downloaded from the internet that are not signed. If you trust the source of the download, remove the block with the following line, and then check again:

xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Users/yourname/BayesTraits/BayesTraitsV5

3. Check that InNOutBT and treeio are installed in R. The package treeio is used to read the tree in the first R script and is available from Bioconductor:

#install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("treeio")

4. Check in the Terminal that pandoc is available, because it is needed to write the Word table. If the following line returns FALSE, install pandoc:

Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::pandoc_available()'

Editing the project files

Open each of the following files in any text editor, such as RStudio.

5. In the main shell script BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh, set:

  • PROJECTFOLDER: the path to the project folder;
  • BAYESTRFOLDER: the path to the folder that contains the BayesTraits executable file, not the path to the file itself;
  • EMAIL: your e-mail address, to receive a message when the analyses start and finish. This depends on your computer being set up to send e-mail with the mail command, but the analyses will run even if the message is not sent.
PROJECTFOLDER="/Users/yourname/BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project"
BAYESTRFOLDER="/Users/yourname/BayesTraits"
EMAIL="your.address@example.com"

6. In the R script 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, set the same BayesTraits folder again, as well as the name of the executable file. Both paths to the BayesTraits folder must be identical:

BayesTraits_dir = "/Users/yourname/BayesTraits",
BayesTraits_exe = "BayesTraitsV5",

7. For your own study, also edit the three numbered R scripts as described in the articles mentioned above, and replace the files in the Data folder. To check that everything works before a long analysis, you can first set a few iterations in 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, such as bi = "2000", it = "12000", sa = "500", and st = c("10", "200"). These values are only for testing, so set your final values again before the real analysis.

Running the analysis

8. Open the Terminal and move to the project folder:

cd /Users/yourname/BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project

9. Allow the main shell script to run. You need to do this only once:

chmod 777 BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh

10. Start the full analysis:

./BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh

Keep the Terminal open and the computer awake until the script finishes. With the number of iterations in the example scripts, this can take a long time.

What the script does

The main shell script then performs the following steps, with no further action from you:

1. Runs 1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R, which saves the input files in the folder results_BayesTraits_phyreg_input;

2. Runs 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, which saves the run commands in the folder results_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell and copies them to the BayesTraits folder, with the data and tree files;

3. Moves to the BayesTraits folder and runs all the analyses, removing the copied files at the end;

4. Moves the results to the folders BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs_log_stone and BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs_sch_trees in the project folder;

5. Runs 3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R, which saves the final table and the heatmaps in the folder results_BayesTraits_phyreg_output, within a subfolder named with the current date, and opens these files.

If something goes wrong

The script continues after an error, so one problem can produce many messages. Look at the first error in the Terminal, because the later ones are often just consequences.

Message Likely cause and solution
chmod: BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh: No such file or directory You are not in the project folder. Repeat step 8.
cannot open file '.../run_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell_unix.sh' BayesTraits_dir is wrong in 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R. See step 6.
cd: no such file or directory BAYESTRFOLDER is wrong in the main shell script. See step 5.
killed, or many mv: rename ...Log.txt ...: No such file or directory messages BayesTraits did not run. macOS may have blocked it (step 2), or BayesTraits_exe is wrong (step 6).
Error in combinat::combn(fnames, 2) : n < m There are no results to process, because BayesTraits did not run. Solve the first error shown.



Creating a Windows PowerShell project folder

In the shell.phyreg.proj function, you can set any path on your PC and the argument syst = "windows" to readily create the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project with associated example files (R scripts, PowerShell script, and data folder) for running the phylogenetic regressions of the Vataireoid legumes on a Windows PC. But then you can easily modify such available scripts for your specific analyses.

library(InNOutBT)

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = "C:/Users/Matt_/Documents",
                  syst = "windows")

After running the shell.phyreg.proj function, it will readily create the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project, a data folder with the input data files vataireoids_1610_25May2022_BayesTraits.csv and vatcomb30_24May22_Yule.con.tree, as well as the main PowerShell script BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1 and R scripts 1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R, 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, and 3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R.



You should see the associated articles on how to set the parameters to create input files with phyreg.inputs for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to create the internal shell script with phyreg.shell for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to process the resulting output files with phyreg.outputs. In these articles, you will find how to fully edit the R scripts 1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R, 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, and 3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R according to your particular study. Otherwise, if you run the example files with the same parameter settings, you will be able to fully reproduce the analysis of our Vataireoid legume study.

The main PowerShell script file BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1 performs the full phylogenetic regression analyses and processing of results. Its first lines hold the paths to your folders and programs, as shown in the image below, which you will set in the next section. The paths in the image are examples from an earlier version of BayesTraits and R, so yours will be different.



Running the Windows PowerShell script

As in Unix, you always start the analysis from the project folder, and the main PowerShell script moves to the BayesTraits folder by itself. You may also want to find further information on how to use Windows PowerShell.

Editing the project files

1. In the main PowerShell script BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1, set $PROJECTFOLDER to the path of the project folder, and $BAYESTRFOLDER to the path of the folder that contains the BayesTraits executable file. Also set the paths to the Rscript, Adobe Acrobat, and Microsoft Word executable files in $RFOLDER, $ACROBATFOLDER, and $WORDFOLDER;

2. In the R script 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, set BayesTraits_dir to the same path as $BAYESTRFOLDER, and BayesTraits_exe to the name of the executable file, such as "BayesTraitsV5";

Running the analysis

3. Open PowerShell as Administrator;

4. Move to the project folder BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project, i.e. the same where you should have the main PowerShell script BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1;

5. Execute the following line and choose option [Y]Yes;
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine

6. Execute the following line:
Unblock-File -Path .\BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1

7. Then perform the full R and BayesTraits run using the PowerShell script by executing the following line:
.\BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1
